texts.preamble: Gurram Subbarao vs State Of A.P., Rep By Pp., on 5 January, 2024 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice V.Srinivas Criminal Revision Case No.982 of 2009 Order:
texts.facts: 3. The shorn of necessary facts are that: i). On 07.03.2002, P.W.1/A.Rameswaram, Food Inspector inspected the shop of petitioner at Allur Village and found sunflower oil was kept in open tin for sale. Then, he purchased 450 grams of sunflower oil, divided the same into three parts, filled the same in three clean, dry and empty bottles, sealed them as per procedure and sent one sample bottle to the Public Analyst, Hyderabad and deposited the remaining two sample bottles with the Local Health Authority and subsequently, he received report from the analyst stating that the sunflower oil contains cotton seed oil also, thereby it was adulterated. ii). Thereafter, he sent proposals to the Director, Institute of Preventive Medicine, Hyderabad and obtained sanction orders to prosecute the petitioner and prepared complaint and filed the complaint before the Court of learned Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Kovur. 4. The said complaint was taken on file and numbered as C.C.No.558 of 2002 and before the trial Court, P.Ws.1 and 2, who are complainant and mediator, were examined and Exs.P.1 to P.23 were exhibited on behalf of the prosecution. No oral and documentary evidence was adduced on behalf of the petitioner/accused. 7. Against the said judgment of the first Appellate Court, the present criminal revision case was preferred by the petitioner/accused.
texts.arguments: In order to decide the above point, Section 11(4) of the Act has to be keep in mind, which is as follows: "An article of food seized under sub-section (4) of section 10, unless destroyed under sub-section (4A) of that section, and any adulterant seized under sub-section (6) of that section shall be produced before a magistrate as soon as possible and in any case not later than seven days after the receipt of the report of the public analyst. Provided that if an application is made to the magistrate in this behalf by the person from whom any article of food has been seized, the magistrate shall by order in writing direct the food inspector to produce such article before him within such time as may be specified in the order" 11. It is clear from the above Act, which mandates that any adulterant seized shall be produced before a Magistrate not later than seven days after the receipt of the report of the Public Analyst 12. 19. More so, this Court in Food Inspector v. Gunturu Venkateswara Rao1 observed regarding these facts and held that Section 11 (4) of the Act has to be followed mandatorily as well polythene bag or bottle cannot be called as a container. 1 2008 (3) ALT (Cri) 238 Gurram Subbarao vs State Of A.P., Rep By Pp., on 5 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115587776/ 3 20.
